text:
alex: Heads-up — planning a regional driver + CUDA bump on Dedicated tomorrow 10:00 PT for us-west-2. Delta is nvidia-driver 535.86 + CUDA 12.2. Want to run a focused safety canary first (small subset, H100B and A100v5 ranges).

maya: Are we sure about 535.x on the older A100v4 hosts? Last time we saw mismatched kernel modules on those boxes.

jin: Good catch. A100v4 in us-west-2 still on kernel-5.15, we had fallback issues before (nv_peer_mem + nvidia-modprobe mismatches). We should exclude v4 from canary or boot them with updated kernel during a separate window.

sam: Suggest canary plan: 6 nodes total, spread across two racks, mix H100B (2), A100v5 (2), A100v4 (0) for canary. Traffic: 5% of dedicated capacity, ramp 10% every 15m if health checks pass.

alex: +1. Add NCCL test suite and distributed small-batch inference smoke. Also run high-IO embedders to exercise NVLink.

maya: Also run a networking MTU sweep — last NCCL hangs in eu-west were traceable to jumbo/frame mismatch from an intermediate switch. Add explicit MTU check to the canary probe.

ops-bot: [automated] rollout_job created: id=rj-20260312-44, target=us-west-2-dedicated, strategy=phased-canary, canary_nodes=6, step_interval=15m.

deploy-bot: [CI] canary image: inference-runtime:2026-03-12-rc3, kernel-modules: 535.86, smoke-tests: nccl_allreduce, grpc-latency.

jin: Adding the exact smoke test commands here so SRE can copy-run:
```
# NCCL smoke test (small world)
python -m infra.tests.nccl_smoke --nodes 6 --iter 50 --msgsize 1M
# GPU stress
./bin/gpu_stress -d 300 -p all
# Health check (curl to local probe)
curl -f http://localhost:9090/health || exit 1
```

sam: We should gate rollback on two signals: 1) >3% increase in p99 latency for text-gen routes, 2) >1.5x memory error counts (CUDA OOM or illegal instruction) or any NCCL collective failures. If either triggers, abort and roll back across region.

maya: And cost gating: if token cost per request increases more than 8% during canary (due to unexpected CPU falling back), abort. Send alerts to #oncall and paging policy.

alex: For rollback choreography: Plan A — automated immediate rollback if NCCL collective fails on any canary node; Plan B — manual hold if only latency blips show (we'll let oncall investigate for up to 30m). Documented steps:
1) stop rollout: POST /api/rollouts/rj-20260312-44/abort
2) trigger driver rollback job: rj-rollback-535.72 -> roll through same nodes
3) run validation smoke tests, if pass, resume traffic; if fail, escalate to eng-infra emergency channel and open incident.

jin: Note — rollback must preserve the exact libcudnn/cuBLAS symlinks. We saw a previous rollback where cuBLAS symlink was left pointing at a newer lib and caused runtime crashes. Add a post-rollback symlink check: `ldd inference_server | grep libcublas`

ops-bot: [automated checklist] pre-canary validations: kernel-headers installed (yes), nvidia-modprobe config checksum ok (sha256: a3f5...), switch MTU verified (1500), NFS mounts RW, monitoring hooks deployed.

sam: Can we also isolate a low-IO path? The problem last time only showed under NVLink-heavy embeddings. Run a second canary with synthetic NVLink-only traffic during the 3rd window.

maya: Agree. Schedule timeline:
- 10:00: prechecks + snapshot node state
- 10:15: deploy to canary nodes (6)
- 10:30: start traffic ramp to 5%
- 10:45: NVLink stress round 1 + MTU sweep
- 11:15: evaluate metrics; if green, continue ramp to 20% and expand to additional rack subset
- 12:00: decision point to proceed region-wide or abort

alex: Who's oncall at 10:00? @sam you're on primary, @jin you are secondary, @maya - you're ops lead for the window. Please confirm.

sam: I can take primary. I'll be by my laptop, pager on.

jin: Secondary confirmed. I'll monitor NCCL logs (elk query: `kubernetes.container_name:inference AND message:/NCCL/`) and keep an eye on kernel oops.

maya: Ops lead confirmed. I'll coordinate the rollback steps and ensure CS/AMs get a heads-up if we need to extend maintenance.

alex: One more risk — some Private deployments share a subset of the same inventory (on-prem nodes mirrored in our inventory). We'll tag the canary to avoid touching anything labeled `private-shared`. Add tag exclusion in the rollout job.

deploy-bot: [action] rollout_job updated: exclude_tags=["private-shared","a100v4"], health_gates=[nccl_allreduce_success, p99_textgen<=1200ms, cpu_fallback_rate<=1.08x], abort_webhook=https://hooks.redwood/internal/rollout/abort

maya: Great. After the canary, we need a short write-up for infra-announce and runbook update. I'll draft the short postmortem template now (if we pass it's a short note; if we fail we follow incident postmortem cadence).

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll kick off the prechecks 09:30 PT and post status in this thread. If anything looks weird, shout and we'll abort early. :thumbsup:
